newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded diffs continue slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded diffs continue slide.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline differentials continued to move lower late Monday in the Chicago and Group Three cash markets, traders said.
The easing differentials combined with sharply lower front-month unleaded futures to fuel a steep drop in spot prices in the Midwest market for the day.

The Midwest differentials fell on perceptions of plentiful stocks in the region, while the NYMEX petroleum complex was moving lower on easing tensions in the Mideast and an apparently bogus report of pressure on Saudi Arabia to boost crude production.
Group Three unleaded gasoline was bid 0.25 cent under the print for prompt deliveries and 0.75 cent under for later deliveries.
Chicago unleaded was talked 0.50/0.75 cent over the print for prompt deliveries and 0.50 cent under the print for later deliveries.
Prompt low sulphur diesel was bid 2.50 cents over the print in Group Three and 1.25 cents over in Chicago, with high sulphur steady in both markets.
Jet/kero was unchanged in both markets.
Discussion was quieted by a Williams pipeline outing in Oklahoma, which pulled some key players out of the market, traders said.
